title: Sauptika: the night massacre
hook: three men are all that's left of an army, and a dying king makes one of them its commander

segments.voice: Yesterday closed Shalya, the war's last day: Balarama's anger, two lists of wrongs, and flowers falling on the man who lost. Your line was let the flowers fall where they fall. Did you notice who wasn't celebrating? Today a new book opens. Day eight hundred forty-nine.

Evening on the battlefield. Three warriors come looking for their king. Ashvatthama, the son of Drona. Kripa, the old teacher of the princes. Kritavarma, a fighter from Krishna's own clan who fought on the other side. They're the last of the Kaurava army still standing. They find Duryodhana where Bhima left him, on the ground, his thighs broken, covered in dust, unable to rise. The man who once commanded a vast host now has three men and a darkening sky. Today, the start of Sauptika, the book of the night, and the strange ceremony held beside a dying king.
screen: `THREE WARRIORS LEFT.` → `THEY FIND THEIR KING.` → `THE BOOK OF THE NIGHT.`

segments.voice: In Ganguli's telling, the three weep at the sight of him. Duryodhana, in pain, still speaks like a king. He tells them not to grieve, that he fought and didn't turn his back, and that this is the way of the world. But Ashvatthama can't let it rest. His grief runs into something older. He remembers how his own father, Drona, died: told a lie about his son's death, laying down his weapons, and then killed. Now he sees his king broken by a blow below the waist. He makes a vow before Duryodhana, in effect: before this night is over, I'll send the Panchalas to the land of the dead. Hear what Duryodhana does next. He can't stand. He has no army. And he asks Kripa to bring a pot of water. With that water, lying in the dust, he has Kripa install Ashvatthama as commander of the army. Of what army? Of three men. The ceremony is real to them anyway. Ashvatthama embraces the king, and the three go off into the night, and Duryodhana is left alone on the field. It's a small scene, almost quiet, but everything in this book grows out of it. A vow made in grief. A title given by a man who has nothing left to give. And a commander with no one to lead but two companions and his own anger.
screen: `THEY WEEP OVER THE KING` · `DRONA'S DEATH REMEMBERED` · `ASHVATTHAMA'S VOW` · then, large: `A COMMANDER OF THREE`

segments.voice: Sit quietly and let the evening of the story settle around you. Bring to mind a time when grief or hurt made you want to promise something big. Breathe in, and feel where that heat sits in your body: the chest, the jaw, the hands. Breathe out, and let the heat cool a little, without pushing it away. Nothing has to be decided now. Just notice how fast a sorrow can turn into a vow. If you pray, you can rest that sorrow in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Sauptika. The book of the night: three survivors, a broken king, a vow, and a commander made with a pot of water.
Your line: an army of three. Today, if a hurt makes you want to promise something, wait an hour before you say it. Day eight hundred forty-nine.

howItsDone: Sauptika, from a Sanskrit word for sleep, is the name of the tenth of the Mahabharata's eighteen books, and reciters of the whole epic carry the story straight on from the fallen king into the night raid.

fork.setup: you're Duryodhana, lying broken on the field. Ashvatthama has just vowed to strike the Panchalas tonight. what do you do?
options: tell him to let the war end.
ask Kripa for water and make Ashvatthama commander.
send him to make peace with the Pandavas.
fork.reveal: he has Kripa bring a pot of water and installs Ashvatthama as commander, though only three men are left.

original.note: commander of the army: the title Duryodhana gives Ashvatthama with a pot of water.

trapdoor: what you thought: the war ended with the mace fight.
what it means: a new book begins that same evening, with a vow made beside the fallen king.
what a scholar hears: the ceremony with the water pot mirrors a real installation rite, held with almost nothing, so the night attack begins as a formal command.

notes: Audit pass: replaced a generic howItsDone (it only restated the plot) with the book's place as the tenth of eighteen parvas and the root of its name in sleep (supta); confirm. Story details checked; no other change.

All paraphrase. In Ganguli the finding of Duryodhana, Ashvatthama's vow and the installation with the water pot fall at the very end of the Shalya Parva, just before the Sauptika Parva opens; the lesson frames them as the start of the night story. Confirm.
Confirm that Kripa performs the installation at Duryodhana's request and that the vow names the Panchalas.
'Kritavarma from Krishna's own clan' (the Vrishni/Satvata Yadavas): confirm wording.
